lines.text: He opened the back door of a jetliner in flight. And jumped.
With two hundred thousand dollars in ransom.
November 24th, 1971. Flight three-oh-five.
A passenger ticketed as Dan Cooper handed a flight attendant a note.
It claimed he had a bomb.
He'd demanded that cash. And four parachutes.
In Seattle, he swapped the passengers for the cash.
Then he ordered the jet south, toward Mexico.
Over southwest Washington, in a storm, he lowered the rear stairs.
And stepped off into the dark.
No trace of him was ever found.
In 1980, an eight-year-old smoothed sand for a campfire by the Columbia River.
Under it: three rotting bundles of twenties.
About five thousand eight hundred dollars. The serial numbers matched the ransom.
But that sandbar sits miles from where investigators think he jumped.
Washed downstream? Buried? Nobody has proven how it got there.
The rest has never been found.
After copycats, the FAA had seven-twenty-sevens fitted with a stair lock.
They call it the Cooper vane.
In 2016, the FBI stopped actively investigating.
No one was ever charged.
Did he die in those woods, or walk out?
Where do you think he landed?
All anyone knows for sure is this.
